newsitem.title: INDIA: Afghan president Rabbani north of Kabul - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Afghan president Rabbani north of Kabul - envoy.

text.p: Afghanistan's ambassador to India said on Friday that President Burhanuddin Rabbani and members of his government were about 25 km (15 miles) north of the capital, Kabul.
"President Rabbani and members of his government are located 25 kilometres off the north of Kabul," Masood Khalili told a news conference in New Delhi.
The envoy said Rabbani's government still controlled 13 of Afghanistan's 31 provinces.
Rabbani's forces, centred on the Bagram airbase, 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul, would now regroup and consider their new military strategy, Khalili said.
The envoy's statement contradicted Taleban commanders who said they controlled the airbase as well as the disused Kabul airport.
"Now they will decide how and when they should launch or enforce their military strategy against Taleban," Khalili said.
Kabul's dramatic overnight collapse was the result of a considered decision by the Rabbani government not to endanger the lives of the city's 1.5 million civilian population, the ambassador said.
"We defended the civilians of Kabul to the last minute," Khalili said. "When we saw they would perish we stopped it."
About 3,000 of Rabbani's troops on the sourthern flank of Kabul retreated to avoid endangering civilians, Khalili said.

Khalili said he was confident the government would push the Taleban from Kabul with forces posted on the heights to the north and northwest of the city. Government forces were still as close as seven km (four miles) from the capital, he said.
He said they were at Pagham resort to the west, at Shakardarra to the northwest and at Dehderra to the north and northeast. He did not specify how many troops there were.
Khalili accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban and accused the Islamic militia of seeking a military instead of a political solution.
Pakistan says it has a neutral position on the civil war.

"The Kabul government has made unfounded allegations of Pakistani interference," a Pakistani foreign ministry spokesman told reporters on Thursday. "We reject these accusations with the contempt they deserve."
"Province after province was captured during the night with the speed of light because during the night the Pakistani forces did not want to be seen by the Afghan government or people," Khalili said.

In a reference to General Rashid Dostum in the north and Karim Khalili, two warlords in the central areas, the envoy said he was confident that President Rabbani's government would survive and defeat the Taleban.
